draftQuestions.question: According to the March 2025 NTIA/NASA 18 GHz Band Report, why did the existing G117 military-only limit on federal FSS not itself restrict ISS? What separate restriction on federal ISS space-to-space links and what NTIA Manual update did the report recommend? Did the report settle non-federal ISS allocation priority as definitively primary? Answer only what this dated report said and cite its original pages.
draftQuestions.draftAnswer: The report says G117 limits federal Fixed Satellite Service (FSS) to military systems, while Inter-Satellite Service (ISS) is a different service class. It recommends a new U.S. footnote limiting federal space-to-space links in this band to communications with a non-federal network or system for space relay, and updating the NTIA Manual with ePFD/PFD limits to protect incumbent operations when the allocation changes are made. It recommends seeking comment on whether non-federal ISS allocations should be primary or secondary; it recommends co-primary allocations in the federal table. These are the report's recommendations, not proof that later FCC rules adopted them.
